reason: The text describes the Israelites groaning and crying out under Egyptian slavery (וַיִּזְעָ֑קוּ - they cried out), and explicitly states that God heard their groans (וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־ נַאֲקָתָ֑ם). God's response to their voicing of suffering is compassionate: He remembers His covenant (וַיִּזְכֹּ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־ בְּרִית֔וֹ), sees the people, and promises deliverance through Moses and Aaron. There is no indication of anger; rather, the passage demonstrates God's mercy and commitment to rescue. Moses also expresses his own doubts and feelings to God, and God responds by empowering him, not by displaying anger.
